abstract: Currarino syndrome is a rare condition with an incidence of approximately 1 in 100,000. It is characterised by the triad of a sacral defect, a presacral mass and anal atresia or stenosis, and it is commonly associated with genetic mutations in the MNX1 gene.We report a case of an infant presenting with recurrent right gluteal abscess secondary to an infected sacrococcygeal teratoma, associated with anal stenosis. Extensive workup was performed to investigate for the source of her recurrent gluteal abscess and anal stenosis, leading to the diagnosis of Currarino syndrome. She underwent multiple surgical procedures, including excision of the infected teratoma, and remains on multidisciplinary surveillance for disease recurrence.Although sacrococcygeal teratomas are not uncommon, they rarely present as gluteal abscesses. Such atypical presentations are difficult to diagnose and can mimic common acute surgical conditions. We discuss the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges faced when managing such cases.
abstract_ja: Currarino症候群は約10万人に1人の希少疾患で、仙骨欠損、仙骨前部腫瘤、肛門閉鎖または狭窄の3徴候を特徴とし、しばしばMNX1遺伝子変異と関連します。我々は、感染した仙尾部奇形腫に続発する再発性右殿部膿瘍と肛門狭窄を呈した乳児を報告します。膿瘍の原因と肛門狭窄の評価のための詳細な検査の結果、Currarino症候群と診断されました。患者は奇形腫の切除を含む複数回の外科的処置を受け、再発のために多職種による経過観察を続けています。仙尾部奇形腫は珍しくないものの、殿部膿瘍として発症することはまれです。このような非典型的な症状は診断が困難で、一般的な急性外科疾患と類似することがあります。本稿では、これらの症例の診断および治療上の課題を考察します。
